question.problem:
A plant spends $C(x)=150+20x+24{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}$ thousands of dollars to produce $x$ units of a certain product per month. The plant sells the product for $$200\,000$ per unit. Given that the plant can produce between $2$ and $9$ units per month, how many units should the plant produce per month to maximize its profit?

The optimal number of plant production is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we apply the candidates test.

First, note that for selling $x$ units of the product, the plant has a revenue (income) of $R(x)=200\cdot x=200x$ thousands of dollars.

Therefore, the profit function (in thousands of dollars) is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x) & =R(x)-C(x) \\  & =200x-(150+20x+24{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}) \\  & ={x}^{3}-24{x}^{2}+180x-150.\end{aligned}
$$

We note that the permitted domain is $2\le x\le 9.$ Therefore, $x=2$ and $x=9$ are candidates for the global maxima of $P(x).$

We need to find the critical points of $P(x)$ for $2<x<9.$ Taking the derivative, we get

$$
{P}^{′}(x)=3{x}^{2}-48x+180,
$$

and solving ${P}^{′}(x)=0$ gives the following critical point:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{′}(x) & =0 \\ 3{x}^{2}-48x+180 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-16x+60 & =0 \\ (x-6)(x-10) & =0 \\ x & =6,10\end{aligned}
$$

Among the critical points $x=6$ and $x=10,$ only $x=6$ is within the permitted domain.

All that's left now is to check if $x=6$ gives a maximum value of $P(x).$ To do this, we compute the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{″}(x) & =6x-48 \\ {P}^{″}(6) & =-12<0\end{aligned}
$$

Since the second derivative at $x=6$ is negative, the point $x=6$ is indeed a maximum.

Our candidates are $x=2,x=6$ and $x=9.$ Computing $P(x)$ at each of these values, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2) & =(2)^{3}-24(2)^{2}+180(2)-150=122 \\ P(6) & =(6)^{3}-24(6)^{2}+180(6)-150=282\,✓ \\ P(9) & =(9)^{3}-24(9)^{2}+180(9)-150=255\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the plant will have a maximum profit level when it produces $6$ units per month.
